newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico man jailed in football slashing case.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico man jailed in football slashing case.

text.p: An Albuquerque dentist was sentenced to two days in jail on Monday for filing the buckles of his son's football helmet down to a razor-sharp edge to slash opposing team players.
Stephen Cito, a children's dentist, was found guilty of conspiring to cause assault with a deadly weapon and was ordered to perform 400 hours of community service.
Mike Cito, 17, escaped jail time but was sentenced to 12 months probation and 100 hours of community service on similar charges at a juvenile court.

Cito, an offensive lineman at St. Pius X High School, cut two opposing players and a referee with the sharpened buckles during a football game in October. One of the players needed 10 stitches to close a cut on his forearm.
Cito was expelled from school and barred from inter-scholastic competition for a year.

Both father and son pleaded no contest to the charges, but Stephen Cito's attorney, Jim Brandenburg, told the court his client had sharpened the helmet buckles to stop opposing players from slapping his son on the head rather than to deliberately cause injury.
"I think this whole thing has been blown out of proportion. I don't mean to justify what they did, but kids playing football have been hurt a great deal more," Brandenburg said.
